excerpt: Originally conceived as a silent visual poem by Philippe Garrel in 1968, Le Révélateur emerged in the aftermath of the May ’68 student uprisings, carrying their disillusionment in a stark, non-verbal form. Shot in austere black and white, the film follows a couple and a child moving through ominous landscapes, from dense forests to barren, almost post-apocalyptic terrains.
